# coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-flash-core-low-delivery-timing

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

Tests **Message Delivery Timing** in isolation on the 10-pair `core` subset with `vertex_ai/gemini-3-flash-preview` (`low` thinking, 100 steps, compaction at 28K, per-turn step counter). Non-blocking incoming peer messages are buffered up to 4 steps until a natural workflow boundary (a passing test, git, or pull-request command, a messaging turn, or an exploration-to-editing shift; blocking `--wait` calls bypass the buffer immediately). Compared directly against `coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-flash-core-low-stepcounter` (4/10 overall, 3/10 clean-merge, 6 merge conflicts).

## Observations

- Passed rose from 4/10 to 5/10 (`$3.25` vs. `$3.70`, 0 API retries), and clean-merge passes rose from 3/10 to 4/10 (`dottxt_ai_outlines_task/1655`, `llama_index_task/17244`, `pallets_jinja_task/1559`, and reconciled `identical` branches on `typst_task/6554`; `openai_tiktoken_task/0` passed via single-branch fallback).
- Merge conflicts dropped in half from 6 to 3: `go_chi_task/27` (a same-function overlap pair) and `pallets_jinja_task/1559` shifted from `conflicts` to `clean` merges, and `pallets_click_task/2800` and `typst_task/6554` converged to `identical` branches.
- Combined across `flash_10` and `core` (20 pairs), `delivery-timing` achieved the highest clean-merge pass count (`8/20` vs. `6/20` baseline) and lowest conflict count (`5/20` vs. `9/20` baseline) among all `gemini-3-flash-preview` arms, earning selection for the 50-pair `flash` confirmation run.
